description: Trigger evals for autonomous-board: it fires on a read-only, glanceable status view of an autonomous run (slices by column, gates, live-run line), while sync-task-state, where-we-at, what-next, portfolio-review and autonomous-readiness handle writing state, a normal task checkpoint, routing, a cross-task board, and the boot check.

should_trigger: show me the board for last night's run

The overnight run on the export task should be finished by now. I don't want to open every file, just lay out which slices are still to-do, which are waiting on me, and which have a diff sitting there for me to merge.
Give me a kanban-style view of the unattended run on the search-indexing task: one row per slice with its complexity and whether the exit criterion is met. Read only, please, do not touch any file.
Is the autonomous run still alive? Check the runs feed for this task and tell me the current step and when it last updated, plus anything stuck at a gate.
quick glance at where the supervised run stands, columns only

should_not_trigger.prompt: The run finished two slices and hit a boundary I resolved by hand. Update TASK_STATE.md so it records that and the next step.
This is a normal three-phase task done by hand, no unattended run involved. Where do we stand against the approved plan and what is still missing to finish?
I don't care about the columns. Just tell me the single best command to run next on this task and in which editor mode.
I have six tasks open across three projects. Rank them by whose move it is and flag any that went quiet or are finished but not archived.

Give me a status of the search-indexing project before tonight. I don't mean what a run did, since none has started yet. I mean whether each item needed to leave it running unattended is covered, with a go or no-go I can trust and a list of any gaps.
